evidence.title: Clayton County BOS extends moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the moratorium (originally set to expire Dec. 31, 2025) was extended by the Board of Supervisors at its Dec. 2, 2025 meeting through Dec. 31, 2026, matching the inventory's recorded extension.
evidence.quote: the supervisors, at their Dec. 2 meeting, approved extending the moratorium until Dec. 31, 2026.

evidence.title: Clayton County Supervisors hold information session on Bitcoin data center
evidence.supports: As of July 21, 2026, no permanent data-center ordinance has replaced the moratorium; a proposed Bitcoin data center still cannot be built and the county is only holding an informational session, consistent with the data-center moratorium (through Dec. 31, 2026) still being the operative restriction alongside the county's existing noise ordinance.
evidence.quote: In Clayton County you have to be below 50 decibels at night, and right now the substation itself puts out more than that.

decisions.notes: The Dec. 31, 2026 extended expiration date has not passed as of the 2026-07-31 research date, so no successor instrument exists yet. The July 21, 2026 KCRG story shows the county still has not adopted a permanent data-center-specific ordinance; the noise-decibel limit cited is part of the county's pre-existing general noise ordinance, not a replacement for the moratorium. Record left unchanged.

outcome.from: County is drafting permanent UDO standards on siting, noise, water use, and review process [VERIFY: as of 2026-04-29 no captured record of UDO data-center standards being adopted. Moratorium remains in effect through 2026-11-08 per Resolution No. 11-06-25-01.]
outcome.to: County is drafting permanent UDO standards on siting, noise, water use, and review process. As of July 22-23, 2026, Johnson County supervisors and the Planning and Zoning Commission were still discussing policy direction for a proposed data-center ordinance (described as one of the more restrictive in eastern Iowa, covering water use, geographic limits, and closed-loop cooling); no ordinance had been adopted. The moratorium remains in effect through 2026-11-08 per Resolution No. 11-06-25-01.
outcome.reason: July 2026 news coverage of a joint Board of Supervisors / Planning and Zoning Commission meeting confirms the UDO data-center standards still had not been adopted as of the last week of July 2026, and the moratorium was still described as governing until its Nov. 8, 2026 expiration.

evidence.supports: Contains the full text of Resolution #21 FYR 25/26, Moratorium on Data Centers, and the roll-call vote adopting it, establishing the formal enactment date, instrument number, and one-year duration.
evidence.quote: RESOLUTION #21 FYR 25/26 - MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTERS: ... NOW on this 25th day of March 2026 ... decisions.notes: Reviewed all 21 Union County board-minutes PDFs from 2026-03-04 through 2026-07-22 (downloaded and text-extracted); 'moratorium' or 'data center' language appears only in the 2026-03-04, 2026-03-11, 2026-03-18, and 2026-03-25 minutes, with no later rescission, extension, or replacement recorded.
